items.briefing:
Home batteries and solar systems connected to the internet are now being flagged as a cybersecurity compliance concern for Australian organisations. If your workplace uses on-site energy storage, it may need to be assessed under existing security frameworks. Separately, AI tools are creating new challenges for traditional security controls, with experts warning that AI-driven systems can behave in ways that bypass standard protections — something worth raising with your IT team if your organisation is adopting AI tools.

There are no immediate threats targeting Australian individuals from today's other reported incidents. **Practical tip:** If your workplace has smart energy systems, ask your facilities or IT team whether those devices are included in your organisation's security reviews.

featured.title: Australia's home batteries are now a cybersecurity compliance isue
featured.summary: Millions of rooftop batteries are now subject to mandatory cyber standards as Canberra widens scrutiny of grid-connected home devices.
